# IOC Extractor 0.1.0

Version 0.1.0 was the first public release of IOC Extractor. This file is a
retrospective, structure-normalized archive of the published
[GitHub Release](https://github.com/xORex-LC/ioc-extractor/releases/tag/v0.1.0).
It was not present in the tagged source tree, and the published release metadata
and artifact remain read-only.

## Highlights

- Refanging of common defanged IOC forms such as `hxxp[:]//`, `[.]` and `[:]`
  through ordered configuration rules.
- IOC detection with RE2/J by default and a `java.util.regex` fallback.
- Public Suffix List-based classification of network masks into the four
  supported `url_match`/`host_match` variants.
- Source attribution from document section markers.
- Four independently configured reputation-list CSV artifacts.
- Oneshot extraction and a Spring Integration daemon with partitioning,
  aggregation, a file ledger, retry and crash recovery.
- ECS JSON logging, diagnostics ports and build-enforced hexagonal boundaries.
- A Debian 11+ installer and hardened systemd unit.

## Added

- `extract` as the initial public CLI workflow.
- Ordered, configuration-driven refang rules.
- RE2/J-backed extraction for IPv4 addresses, domains, URLs, MD5, SHA-1 and
  SHA-256 indicators.
- Declarative output mapping and independent schemas and ID spaces for:
  - `masks_list_generated.csv`;
  - `ip_list_generated.csv`;
  - `address_blacklist_generated.csv`;
  - `hashes_list_generated.csv`.
- Batch-local de-duplication and CSV lookup support for preserving IDs across
  the original aggregation workflow.
- A file-poll daemon with stability checks, partition output, aggregation,
  retry and a file ledger.
- JDK 21 packaging for Debian hosts.

## Changed

Not applicable. Version 0.1.0 established the first public product contract and
had no earlier published release to change.

## Fixed

Not applicable. Version 0.1.0 was the initial public release rather than an
upgrade or maintenance release.

## Upgrade notes

There was no earlier supported release to upgrade. Version 0.1.0 required a
fresh installation with JDK 21; the supplied installer provisioned Temurin 21
for Debian 11+ hosts.

No cross-version rollback procedure existed yet. Recovery meant reinstalling
the application and restoring any operator-managed input, configuration and CSV
artifacts from an external backup.

## Breaking or observable contract changes

Not applicable relative to an earlier public version. The initial observable
contract consisted of the `extract` CLI, the four CSV artifact schemas, the
oneshot/daemon runtime modes and flat ECS-style structured log fields.

## Known issues

- IOC patterns still needed tightening for `.onion`, IPv6 addresses, email
  addresses and Telegram handles, together with a larger regression corpus.
- STIX/OpenIOC export and Debian package generation were not implemented.
- Hash-aware repeat lookup was planned but absent from the initial CSV lookup
  workflow.

## Verification

The published release stated that `./mvnw verify` passed the unit tests,
ArchUnit boundaries, Maven Enforcer rules and a golden end-to-end extraction
fixture covering the supported classification buckets. The project did not yet
retain the current release-workflow evidence, embedded commit identity or
exact-candidate stand record.

## Artifacts and checksums

The release published one binary artifact:

- [`ioc-app-0.1.0.jar`](https://github.com/xORex-LC/ioc-extractor/releases/download/v0.1.0/ioc-app-0.1.0.jar)

No SHA-256 checksum sidecar was published for version 0.1.0. The current
versioned `ioc-extractor-*.jar` naming and mandatory checksum contract were
introduced after this release and are not claimed retroactively.
